item.title: G20 Chair’s Statement G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

G20 Chair’s Statement G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting

Media Note

October 31, 2026

  1. The G20 Foreign Ministers met in Atlanta, Georgia on October 30 and October 31, 2026, in the 250th year of the United States’ independence. The U.S. presidency has pursued taking the G20 back to basics, focusing on its core mission of discussing global economic challenges and proposing solutions that help improve our citizens’ lives, raise their standards of living, and create economic prosperity for everyone. The ministers held candid discussions on the U.S. priorities. Specifically, ministers discussed energy security, supply chain resilience, and geopolitical tensions, including the Straits of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab.

Energy Security

  1. Every country is sensitive to the price of energy. Every time there is an increase in the price of gasoline, the cost of natural gas to heat a home, or the electricity to power our digital lives, the cost of energy is felt by everyone. No country can have prosperity without energy. Far too often governments have placed barriers to energy production and punished their own people with higher costs. This is why it is not enough to have access to energy; it is important that energy is abundant and access for everyone is affordable. These conditions promote productivity, strengthen industry, improve energy security, and increase economic growth. It is also vital that countries build the infrastructure to develop and deploy the energy systems of the future. Abundant energy is the backbone of a booming economy and the foundation of enduring prosperity.
  1. Energy is a foundational requirement for economic progress. Too often, misguided policies in one part of the world have stifled energy access in another part of the world. At the same time, global energy demand keeps increasing as economies grow, driven by a range of factors, including population growth, economic development, industrialization, electrification, increasing cooling needs, expanding car and truck demand, and the unprecedented rise of digitalization and information technology. Meeting demand in a manner that addresses affordability, accessibility, and security strengthens economic competitiveness and resilience; enhances participation in the global economy; and, critically, people live better, healthier, more prosperous lives.
  1. Further, emerging energy technologies can deliver abundant, baseload energy. Advancements in civil nuclear energy technology, including small modular and micro reactors, can contribute to meeting growing global electricity demand and enhancing energy security. Still, we recognize that, for some, nuclear energy may not be a desired option for their energy mix.
  1. Every country is on its own energy path and each country’s needs will demand different energy sources. One country should not be constrained by what another country decides to use. Every country is entitled to make its own sovereign choices.

Supply Chain Resilience

  1. Global supply chains are crucial for modern societies to thrive. Basic materials like fertilizer are essential for food production and security, raw materials are necessary for basic manufacturing, and critical minerals are crucial for energy security, advanced manufacturing, and emerging technologies.
  1. It is important that G20 members improve the resilience of these supply chains, and it begins with sharing more information, improving transparency, and mobilizing investment. Updating the permitting process and regulations can further expand supply chain efficiency.
  1. Recognizing that governments alone cannot solve this problem, governments should commit to close partnerships with the private sector. Such partnership can help advance processing, refining and recycling of critical minerals. Investment is crucial to strengthening supply chains. Stable and predictable domestic regulatory environments, along with durable contractual frameworks, particularly for long-term agreements, underpin the investments required to expand supply chains for energy and critical minerals.

Geopolitical Tensions

  1. The world has felt the effects of significant global energy disruptions in 2026. It is important to ensure secure, resilient, and uninterrupted energy flows, including safe navigation and transit passage through international waterways and the security of critical infrastructure, as essential to global economic stability and energy security.
  1. Further, the weaponization of normal food supply chains is an increasingly frequent challenge within the trading system, whereby a government takes targeted actions to slow, stop, or block the trade of food in order to exert coercive pressure over another sovereign country on an unrelated geopolitical issue. It is important the global community agree that trade in food and agricultural products should not be used as a tool for economic or political coercion.

Ebola

  1. As Ministers noted, international cooperation is key to combating Ebola. The $2 billion raised to fight the outbreak at the September event in New York, held during the U.S. presidency, has catalyzed a more aggressive response to this deadly disease. The G20 commends the communities and the frontline responders for their tireless efforts.

Sports Diplomacy

  1. Ministers expressed their appreciation to the people of Atlanta and the State of Georgia for their hospitality. It also provided an opportunity for G20 partners to experience the deep American tradition of U.S. football, and one of the greatest collegiate rivalries between the University of Georgia and the University of Florida.
  1. The U.S. G20 Presidency appreciates G20 members’ contributions to our candid, substantive deliberations in Atlanta. We look forward to the Leaders’ Summit in Miami and the presidency of the United Kingdom in 2027.

item.title: Quad Joint Press Release on Economic Prosperity and Security
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Quad Joint Press Release on Economic Prosperity and Security

Media Note

October 31, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Secretary of State of the United States, the Foreign Minister of Australia, the External Affairs Minister of India, and the Foreign Minister of Japan. 

Begin text: 

The Secretary of State of the United States and the Foreign Ministers of Australia, India, and Japan met in Atlanta, Georgia, on October 31, 2026, to discuss progress on ongoing Quad initiatives and reaffirm their commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific. 

The Quad ministers underscored the importance of economic security in maintaining global stability and prosperity.  They reiterated their commitment to building reliable and open global supply chains and trusted and resilient infrastructure.  They expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, as well as non-market policies and practices that result in overcapacity to disrupt global supply chains in critical industries.  Recognizing the importance of critical sea lanes, the uninterrupted flow of commerce, energy security, and the unhindered passage and safety of maritime crews and vessels without the imposition of tolls, they reiterated the absolute necessity to protect and preserve navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in accordance with international law as reflected in UNCLOS.   

The Quad ministers highlighted the importance of Super Intelligence (SI)* and initiatives like Pax Silica to the future of economic growth and expressed their intent to provide over $85 million of technical and financial assistance to support access to trusted SI across the Indo-Pacific, including through the Quad SI Accelerator. 

The Quad ministers expressed their deep concern about the proliferation of online and cyber scams that pose a threat to national and international peace and security.  They condemned the criminal groups running the scam operations and trafficking people and forcing them to defraud our citizens, stealing tens of billions of dollars annually of hard-earned wealth from our respective countries.  The Quad countries committed to dismantling these operations and holding transnational criminal groups and their leaders accountable. 

The Quad ministers expressed their condolences for those who lost their lives during the flash floods of August 26, 2026, and underscored their shared commitment to supporting partners in times of need.  They recognized India’s leading role as the first responder to Nepal’s rescue, along with the significant support to Nepal from all Quad countries. 

The Quad ministers welcomed progress on key initiatives bolstering the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific, including: 

Economic Prosperity and Security 

·       Securing Critical Minerals Supply Chains:  Under the Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework announced in May 2026, Quad countries have strengthened their cooperation on critical mineral supply chains, working together to recover critical minerals from electronics waste and scrap materials to reduce reliance on any single supplier.  They welcomed private sector-led investment in waste collection networks, processing plants, and refineries, and work with Quad countries to establish trusted critical minerals recycling value chains.  They welcomed the U.S. commitment to provide $10 million to promote infrastructure and facilities in India and ASEAN countries that recover critical minerals from waste.  Quad countries look forward to exploring streamlining export and import procedures to facilitate the transboundary movement of recyclable materials and strengthen the implementation of existing regulations. 

·       Supporting Energy Security in the Indo-Pacific:  In September, the Quad convened the first-ever Quad Fuel Security Forum and discussed our commitment to advancing fuel security in the Indo-Pacific, including by strengthening their respective strategic petroleum reserves and stockholdings. 

·       Advancing Ports Infrastructure in Fiji:  Quad countries are actively working with the Government of Fiji on infrastructure modernization projects for key ports at Suva, Lautoka, and Rokobili.  This includes through the U.S. Millennium Challenge Corporation, which is supporting Fiji in developing a Port Strategic Development Framework, and the Government of Australia, which is assessing the feasibility of a new transshipment port facility. 

·       Building Infrastructure Capability Across the Indo-Pacific:  To date, Quad countries have provided more than 2000 infrastructure fellowships across the Pacific, Southeast Asia, and South Asia providing critical skills to Indo-Pacific nations to support a stronger and more resilient region. 

·       Advancing Commercial Diplomacy:  The Quad ministers announced the first-ever Quad Business Leaders’ Forum that will convene industry leaders, government, and policy experts from Quad countries to foster greater ties across our public and private sectors, including the promotion of commercial deals in key sectors.  Quad export credit agencies, building on their 2024 Memorandum of Cooperation, will convene in Tokyo on November 18 to identify opportunities for practical cooperation, further demonstrating our commitment to deepening economic cooperation. 

·       Progressing Secure and Resilient Digital Connectivity in the Indo-Pacific:  Quad countries continue to accelerate efforts to develop trusted, redundant, and high-speed cable routes in the region and share best practices to manage secure and resilient undersea data cables. 

Maritime and Transnational Security 

·       Making the Seas Safer:  The second Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer mission successfully sailed from Chennai, India, to Perth, Australia from September 25 to October 7 with representatives from all four Quad countries aboard an Indian Coast Guard Offshore Patrol Vessel, a significant step toward strengthening Quad maritime interoperability to address unlawful maritime activities. 

·       Strengthening Maritime Collaboration:  The Quad countries look forward to holding their first exercise under the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration initiative at Sea Dragon 2027.  The initiative was announced in May by the Secretary and Foreign Ministers in New Delhi to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness. 

·       Improving Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA):  The Quad countries are pleased to announce the first Quad Maritime Domain Awareness Track 1.5 Symposium under the Quad Maritime Training Initiative (MAITRI) in early 2027, which will provide a platform for regional partners to discuss MDA approaches, technologies, and information sharing. 

Critical and Emerging Technology 

·       Trusted Communications Networks:  In the spirit of the Quad Leaders’ endorsement of the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, Quad countries committed to identifying priority countries for cooperation on trusted advanced communication technologies, including 5G, 6G, Open Radio Access Networks (RAN), and SI* RAN developing a pipeline of trusted 5G projects, as well as exploring future cooperation on SI* RAN. 

·       Semiconductor and SI* Hardware:  Quad countries reinforced the need to build secure, resilient, and trusted supply chains for advanced, leading-edge semiconductors and SI* hardware.  They will launch a new effort to identify semiconductor and SI* supply chain chokepoints before they cause disruptions. 

·       Digital Identity Standards:  Quad countries continue to advance efforts to map digital identity standards, making it easier for our public and private sectors to work together. 

·       Deepening Cooperation on Cyber Security: This month, Quad Cyber Senior Officials met and pledged to continue advancing Quad countries’ unique capabilities to support a trusted and resilient cybersecurity environment in the Indo-Pacific region. 

Humanitarian Assistance and Emergency Response 

·       Building Capacity to Respond to Disasters:  The Quad continues to improve capabilities to respond to natural disasters via its Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief Partnership.  Australia, Japan, and the United States will send observers to India’s Annual Joint Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief Exercise (AJHE-26) in November to build shared capacity to respond to natural disasters. 

·       Developing Shared Logistics Capabilities:  The Quad countries made significant progress toward the development of the Indo-Pacific Logistics Network (IPLN) Standard Operating Procedures, during the second IPLN Tabletop Exercise (TTX) hosted by Japan’s Ministry of Defense in September.  This will facilitate swift and effective response to natural disasters in the Indo-Pacific region.  The Quad countries will continue advancing their shared humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) logistics capacity, including at the next IPLN exercise to be held at the next Rim of the Pacific (RIMPAC) exercise. 

We look forward to the convening of the Quad Leaders’ Summit, the next Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, and continuing our engagements that advance peace, stability, and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific and beyond. 

End text.  

* In Australia, India, and Japan, ‘Super Intelligence’ refers to ‘artificial intelligence.’

item.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting Welcome Reception
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Atlanta, Georgia

Georgia Aquarium

Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting Welcome Reception

Remarks

October 30, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Thank you.  Thank you.  Good evening.  Well, those lights are bright.  Now I can see you.  Anyway.  But good evening, and thank you all for coming, and welcome to Atlanta.  This is what I think has been a very productive start to what I hope will be a very productive ministerial.  

Our job is obviously, as I said earlier today, to create the platform in the – upon which our leaders will be able to meet in a few weeks in Doral and really have a successful G20.  Together, I think that we are mapping a vibrant, dynamic, and bold economic future, one that will pioneer new horizons for the entire world.

So I wanted to take a moment to thank the city of Atlanta for being our host in this spectacular place that I’ve never been to before but is one of the treasures in our country.  The history of Atlanta is a testament to what human ingenuity can achieve.  It was less than 200 years ago, this city – what we know today as Atlanta – was little more than a railroad junction, a wooden stake driven into the clay marking the end of the line.  Its original name was actually Terminus.  That was the name of it, the place where the railway ended, literally stopped.  Within a few decades, of course, it became a thriving center of commerce.  And when the Civil War left the city devastated – it was one of the places that was almost burned down – its people rebuilt it.  And in the generations that followed, they transformed a modest railroad town into one of the great commercial powerhouses in the United States.

Here in Georgia and across the whole of the American South, we see a vision of our economic future taking shape.  It’s alive.  It’s expanding.  It’s on the move.  It’s bursting with limitless possibility.  We see revolutionary inventions and innovations.  Many of the fastest-growing cities in our nation, in the United States, are here in the South.  We see new factories.  We see new businesses.  We see new jobs, both white-collar jobs and blue-collar jobs alike.  We see world-class universities teeming with brilliant, creative students who are preparing, literally as we speak, to lead their country’s future into new frontiers.

The explosion of dynamism, prosperity, and creative energy taking place here is not an accident.  It is the direct result of a series of policy decisions rendered by the leaders of these states.  These were deliberate decisions aimed at giving their businesses, their entrepreneurs, their citizens the opportunities to build, to innovate, and to grow; to provide the economic foundations, the infrastructure, and the regulatory environment needed to unleash the potential of their people.

The economy of the future that Americans are building here in Atlanta and throughout the South – and all across our country, really – can belong to our economic partners and allies and friends as well: a future of economic prosperity and growth that is backed by secure, affordable energy and regulations that encourage innovation and growth in the industries of tomorrow.

Since day one of his term, President Trump has prioritized realizing this vision.  It is in the economic and national security interests of the United States that we are energy dominant, that we have robust supply chains, that we remove the regulatory hurdles that hamper growth, and that we lead in the advancement of super intelligence and other critical emerging technologies.  By the way, I say that’s in our national interest, but I would also argue it’s probably in the national interest of every country represented at this gathering that you also have energy and technology and advancements and innovation and so forth.

It’s also President Trump’s mission and many of your leaders’ missions to see that this group focuses on core economic policy issues.  We want to implement practical solutions, solutions that deliver real, positive results – from our perspective for the American people, from your perspective for the people of your countries, and ultimately of the world. 

As the United States has been host of the G20 this year we’ve held gatherings across the country that have focused on many aspects of our advanced economies, and the topics that have been covered include trade, fiscal and monetary policy, emerging technology, and energy.  This week we maintain that sharp focus on our economic interests, building on our prior meetings, and setting the stage for our leaders and their summit in Doral in just a few weeks.

I’d also like to take a moment to note the inclusion of Poland as a full participant in this G20.  President Trump believes their economic success and growing global influence is exactly what the G20 needs to tackle the major economic challenges we all face, and we’re very excited to have them with us here today and this week.

The economic challenges facing our countries are complex and they are interconnected.  Because we all face these challenges, we must all work together to address them.  The future of our nations depend on our willingness to understand that while our interests may not always align, we should always seek to work together to advance them when and where they do align.  It is in our all of our interests that we commit to doing so.

My team and I want to work with you to ensure that the Leaders’ Summit is as successful as it possibly can be, and it’s my sincere hope that we can lay a solid foundation of aligned commitment and shared focus on policies that advance our common interests and help our nations prosper for generations to come.

So welcome to Atlanta, welcome to the United States.  Thank you.  It’s been very productive.  I look forward again to tomorrow and of course look forward to Doral in just a few weeks.  Thank you very much.  (Applause.)

Here in Georgia and across the whole of the American South, we see a vision of our economic future taking shape.  It’s alive.  It’s expanding.  It’s on the move.  It’s bursting with limitless possibility.  We see revolutionary inventions and innovations.  Many of the fastest-growing cities in our nation, in the United States, are here in the South.  We see new factories.  We see new businesses.  We see new jobs, both white-collar jobs and blue-collar jobs alike.  We see world-class universities teeming with brilliant, creative students who are preparing, literally as we speak, to lead their country’s future into new frontiers.

The explosion of dynamism, prosperity, and creative energy taking place here is not an accident.  It is the direct result of a series of policy decisions rendered by the leaders of these states.  These were deliberate decisions aimed at giving their businesses, their entrepreneurs, their citizens the opportunities to build, to innovate, and to grow; to provide the economic foundations, the infrastructure, and the regulatory environment needed to unleash the potential of their people.

The economy of the future that Americans are building here in Atlanta and throughout the South – and all across our country, really – can belong to our economic partners and allies and friends as well: a future of economic prosperity and growth that is backed by secure, affordable energy and regulations that encourage innovation and growth in the industries of tomorrow.

Since day one of his term, President Trump has prioritized realizing this vision.  It is in the economic and national security interests of the United States that we are energy dominant, that we have robust supply chains, that we remove the regulatory hurdles that hamper growth, and that we lead in the advancement of super intelligence and other critical emerging technologies.  By the way, I say that’s in our national interest, but I would also argue it’s probably in the national interest of every country represented at this gathering that you also have energy and technology and advancements and innovation and so forth.

It’s also President Trump’s mission and many of your leaders’ missions to see that this group focuses on core economic policy issues.  We want to implement practical solutions, solutions that deliver real, positive results – from our perspective for the American people, from your perspective for the people of your countries, and ultimately of the world. 

As the United States has been host of the G20 this year we’ve held gatherings across the country that have focused on many aspects of our advanced economies, and the topics that have been covered include trade, fiscal and monetary policy, emerging technology, and energy.  This week we maintain that sharp focus on our economic interests, building on our prior meetings, and setting the stage for our leaders and their summit in Doral in just a few weeks.

I’d also like to take a moment to note the inclusion of Poland as a full participant in this G20.  President Trump believes their economic success and growing global influence is exactly what the G20 needs to tackle the major economic challenges we all face, and we’re very excited to have them with us here today and this week.

The economic challenges facing our countries are complex and they are interconnected.  Because we all face these challenges, we must all work together to address them.  The future of our nations depend on our willingness to understand that while our interests may not always align, we should always seek to work together to advance them when and where they do align.  It is in our all of our interests that we commit to doing so.

My team and I want to work with you to ensure that the Leaders’ Summit is as successful as it possibly can be, and it’s my sincere hope that we can lay a solid foundation of aligned commitment and shared focus on policies that advance our common interests and help our nations prosper for generations to come.

So welcome to Atlanta, welcome to the United States.  Thank you.  It’s been very productive.  I look forward again to tomorrow and of course look forward to Doral in just a few weeks.  Thank you very much.  (Applause.)

item.title: United States-Japan-Republic of Korea (ROK) Trilateral Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

United States-Japan-Republic of Korea (ROK) Trilateral Foreign Ministers’ Meeting

Readout

October 30, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio met today with Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu and ROK Foreign Minister Cho Hyun on the margins of the G20 in Atlanta to review progress across the trilateral partnership that advances security and prosperity in a free and open Indo-Pacific.  The Secretary and Foreign Ministers signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) for a Trilateral Arctic Pacific Partnership (TAPP) to explore maritime cooperation and economic partnership in the Pacific Arctic.

The Secretary and Foreign Ministers reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) and to full implementation of UN Security Council resolutions (UNSCRs), including the ban on supporting revenue generation for the DPRK’s nuclear and ballistic missile programs.  They commended the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team’s (MSMT) work exposing the DPRK’s violations and evasions of UNSCRs.  They also emphasized the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait.  Secretary Rubio also raised China’s efforts to assert control over the South China Sea, its coercive behavior in the East China Sea and Yellow Sea, and Russia-China cooperation that undermines peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

The Secretary and Foreign Ministers stressed the importance of economic security and reaffirmed their shared opposition to economic coercion and the weaponization of supply chains.  They reviewed implementation of the trilateral Memorandum of Cooperation on Small Modular Reactor Deployments, signed in Ankara July 7, leveraging our combined industrial strengths to advance global energy security.  They also discussed areas of economic security cooperation identified at the October 15 trilateral economic security consultation in Seoul.  

The Secretary and Foreign Ministers reaffirmed the commitments reflected in the U.S.-Japan-ROK trilateral joint statement issued on September 21, 2026 and committed to continuing trilateral meetings at all levels.

item.title: Secretary Rubio Announces U.S. Participation in World Expo 2030 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Secretary Rubio Announces U.S. Participation in World Expo 2030 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

Media Note

October 30, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Faisal bin Farhan signed the participation contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh today on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia.  The signing formalizes U.S. participation in this global event.  

Expo 2030 opens in Riyadh on October 1, 2030, and runs through mid-March 2031.  Saudi Arabia projects more than 42 million visitors from over 200 countries, making Expo 2030 one of the decade’s largest public and commercial diplomacy platforms.  The United States will use Expo 2030 to showcase American innovation, expand commercial opportunities for U.S. businesses, and strengthen the bilateral relationship with Saudi Arabia.  Formalizing participation is the first step in preparation and planning for the USA Pavilion at this key event.

For further information on International Expositions, please email expo@state.gov or find us at usapavilion.us.  For media inquiries, please submit here.

item.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan al Saud at an Expo 2030 Riyadh Participation Contract Signing Ceremony
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State, Prince Faisal bin Farhan al Saud, Saudi Foreign Minister
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Prince Faisal bin Farhan al Saud, Saudi Foreign Minister

Atlanta, Georgia

Loews Atlanta

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan al Saud at an Expo 2030 Riyadh Participation Contract Signing Ceremony

Readout

October 30, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, we’re – thank you all for covering this.  We’re excited to sign this contract that announces the United States formal commitment to Expo 2030, which will be held in Riyadh.  It’s still a few years away, but this is an important first step to prepare for a world-leading USA Pavilion in Riyadh, which we’re very excited about.  This is an opportunity to strengthen our bilateral relationship with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and to showcase America on the global stage and expand commercial opportunities for U.S. businesses.  So thank you for covering it and thank you for allowing us to be a part of it. 

And with that, we’ll sign this.  Do you want to say a few words?

FOREIGN MINISTER AL SAUD: Well, thank you, Marco, and thank you for your engagement and your support for Expo 2030, and we look forward to seeing the U.S. Pavilion and everything you have to offer.

Thank you. 

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Thank you.

(The contract was signed.)

item.title: Joint Statement from the International Contact Group for the Great Lakes Region (ICG)
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement from the International Contact Group for the Great Lakes Region (ICG)

Media Note

October 30, 2026

The United States, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom, as members of the International Contact Group (ICG) for the Great Lakes region, chaired by France, issue the following statement on the situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo:

Begin text.

The International Contact Group for the Great Lakes region (ICG) encourages all parties to the Washington Accords and Doha Framework to remain committed and engage in good faith to find a lasting and peaceful resolution of the conflict and to fulfil their obligations without delay. The ICG supports the efforts of the mediators, including those of the African Union, led by the President of the Council of the Togolese Republic, welcomes the co-facilitators’ recent visit to the region and reaffirms the importance of regional leadership.

In light of recent political and security-related developments in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the ICG welcomes the statement issued on 19 October by the President of the African Union Commission calling on all parties to exercise restraint. The ICG categorically rejects the pursuit of political objectives through the use of violence, as advocated by the recently created Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN).

It underscores the need for all parties to respect the rule of law and the Constitution of the DRC and reiterates its commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the DRC.  It recalls the importance of a peaceful and inclusive inter-Congolese dialogue involving all key Congolese stakeholders as an essential prerequisite for lasting peace in the DRC.  Political differences and grievances cannot be resolved by military means.  Guaranteeing rule of law and protection of fundamental rights is crucial to ensure that all political parties and civil society organizations can freely exercise their role.

The ICG reiterates its deep concern over the continued fighting in eastern DRC and deplores the suffering inflicted on civilian populations. It urges all parties to honor their commitments made in Doha on 19 July 2025 to observe a ceasefire.  The escalating use of drones has grave consequences for civilians and humanitarian workers.

The ICG reminds the parties to implement UN Security Council Resolution 2773, which calls for the Rwanda Defence Forces to cease support to the M23 and immediately withdraw from DRC territory without preconditions, the dismantling of illegitimate parallel administrations in the DRC territory, and the neutralization of the FDLR.  On this last point, recalling the ICG statement of August 14 taking good note of the plan put forward by the DRC government, the ICG encourages the Congolese authorities to present an action plan and timeline aimed at swiftly implementing the disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration protocol for the FDLR groups.

Against the backdrop of increasing humanitarian needs and the Ebola epidemic, the ICG urges all parties and armed groups to respect international humanitarian law and to ensure that humanitarian actors have full, safe and unimpeded access to populations in need.

End text.

item.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio at a Plenary Session on Geopolitical Issues
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Atlanta, Georgia

Secretary of State Marco Rubio at a Plenary Session on Geopolitical Issues

Remarks

October 30, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO: Thank you all for being here. I want to welcome all of you to the city of Atlanta here in Georgia, and this – what I hope will be a productive meeting today as we are – a critical moment. I would call it a moment of choosing, and I would say not just for my country, the United States of America, but frankly for the world.

We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises, many of which pose severe threats – severe threats to essential foundations of the global economic order. New disruptions and strains to global energy and food supplies – and food markets – to the global supply chain, trade, to freedom of navigation itself. And the G20 must work together to confront these threats, to strengthen our economic resilience, to safeguard our markets and the economies that they sustain.

The challenge we have – the challenges we have addressed during the presidency of President Trump are multifaceted and interconnected, and the solutions must be, too. Here we can help set the context for expanded geopolitical stability and the broader economic prosperity agenda that our leaders will tackle. As diplomats, as political leaders, we have a vital role. We are tasked, on behalf of the nations that we serve, to work together with one another to coordinate responses to emerging crises and to protect our shared interests. By translating our shared interest into practical cooperation and real action, we can reinforce global stability – and more importantly, we can deliver meaningful results for our citizens.

We have a lot to cover over the next two days. Briefly, in terms of the modality – the modalities, we’re going to cover two issues in this plenary session: freedom of navigation and food security. I’ll introduce the topic and turn to the next speaker. We’ll go around the table; we’ll do it in alphabetical order. I would ask if you can – I know these are complex and nuanced topics, but if we could limit it to three minutes or so for each intervention, because if we don’t then we’ll be here for a long period of time. And then I’ll wrap up at the end of each topic as we move on to the next topic.
